# LinkButton

`<LinkButton>` is used when you need a link to look like a button. It supports all the visual variations of regular `<Button>` <br />

<em>NB!</em> It is preferred to keep links and buttons looking different to not confuse the user.{" "}

## Usage with common routing frameworks

### React Router v6

React Router v6 removed the `component` prop from `<Link>`. The official suggestion
is to create your own button using hooks provided by React Router.
https://reactrouter.com/docs/en/v6/upgrading/v5#remove-link-component-prop

Create a component using the `<LinkButton>` from Kalep and hooks from React Router:

```typescript
import {LinkProps, useHref, useLinkClickHandler} from "react-router-dom";
import {LinkButton, LinkButtonVisualProps} from "@bolteu/kalep-react";

// Include props that define the looks of the LinkButton
type FancyLinkProps = LinkProps & LinkButtonVisualProps;

const FancyLink = React.forwardRef<HTMLAnchorElement, FancyLinkProps>(
    ({onClick, replace = false, state, target, to, ...rest}, ref) => {
        const href = useHref(to);
        const handleClick = useLinkClickHandler(to, {
            replace,
            state,
            target,
        });

        return (
            <LinkButton
                {...rest}
                href={href}
                onClick={(event) => {
                    onClick?.(event);
                    if (!event.defaultPrevented) {
                        handleClick(event);
                    }
                }}
                ref={ref}
                target={target}
            />
        );
    },
);
```

And then use it just as you would use the original `<Link>` from React Router:

```typescript
<FancyLink to="/about">About</FancyLink>
```

And with customizations from `LinkButton`:

```typescript
import {Heart} from "@bolteu/kalep-react-icons";

<FancyLink to="/about" variant="secondary" endIcon={<Heart />}>
    About
</FancyLink>;
```

### React Router v5

In previous React router versions you can pass the `LinkButton` component to
the React Router `<Link>` in its `component` prop like this:

```typescript
import {Link} from "react-router-dom";
import {LinkButton} from "@bolteu/kalep-react";

<Link to="/about" component={LinkButton}>
    About
</Link>;
```

And with custom settings:

```typescript
import {Link} from "react-router-dom";
import {LinkButton} from "@bolteu/kalep-react";
import {Heart} from "@bolteu/kalep-react-icons";

<Link to="/about" component={(args) => <LinkButton variant="secondary" endIcon={<Heart />} size="sm" {...args} />}>
    About
</Link>;
```

### Next.js

Use the `<LinkButton>` component as the children of Next's `<Link>` component
as described in the official documentation:
https://nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/next/link#if-the-child-is-a-custom-component-that-wraps-an-a-tag

Note that you need to use the `passHref` prop on `Link` like this: `<Link href="/about" passHref>`
otherwise the underlying anchor tag inside `LinkButton` won't receive the href. You can configure
ESLint with the rule `next/link-passhref` to enforce this.

LinkButton with custom settings:

```typescript
<Link href="/about" passHref>
    <LinkButton variant="secondary" endIcon={<Heart />} size="sm">
        About
    </LinkButton>
</Link>
```
